subject: Edge peering blackout — customer switch plan and audit packet
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.example>
To: Acme Retail <ops@acme.com>; CloudInfra Support <support@cloudinfra.example>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.example>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.example>
Date: 2029-05-30T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Edge peering blackout — immediate customer switch plan

Hi Sam and team,

Quick summary: between 07:53–08:06 PDT today a sustained outage on our primary peering fabric with CloudInfra (north-1) caused a sharp increase in connection resets and 502/503 responses for routes terminating in US-West and EU-West. Our control plane detected the degradation at 07:58 and initiated automatic reroutes to our secondary fabric and warm standby endpoints. The majority of traffic recovered to full success by ~08:12, but we observed intermittent elevated latency and a small percentage of requests still failing for customers who have IP-based allowlists or region-locked DNS records.

What we did (summary for ops):
- Executed an emergency route policy to prefer secondary fabric for affected prefixes (07:59).
- Issued real-time configuration to force-region-fallback for customers who opted in (08:01).
- Opened a ticket with CloudInfra (CI-3827) and requested peering checks.

Actions I need from Acme ops to reduce user impact immediately:
1) If you have IP allowlists pointing at our primary ingress ranges, please add the secondary ingress blocks listed in the attached routing script (customer-routing-script.sh).
2) Temporarily enable the API query parameter region_preference=any for background jobs (this will let us finish in-flight requests against fallback endpoints).
3) If you require a DNS-level change, we can provide a short CNAME that points to multi-region ingress (see attachment). We recommend making this change only if you cannot apply an allowlist update.

Attachments: ingress_blackout_summary.pdf (PDF, 220KB) — incident timeline and packet counters
Attachment: customer-routing-script.sh (BASH, 2KB) — sample iptables/dns entries you can apply

We will follow up with a post-incident packet capture and timeline. Please confirm when you apply the allowlist changes so we can monitor your traffic and mark you "fully rerouted" in our incident tracker.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
phone: +1 415-555-0193

From: Sam Patel <ops@acme.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.example>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.example>
Date: 2029-05-30T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Edge peering blackout — immediate customer switch plan

Thanks Priyom — we've started applying the allowlist updates to our edge firewalls now (rolling change). ETA for completion across three datacenters: 20 minutes.

Two quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether the region_preference=any change will preserve ordering of in-flight messages for our ingestion pipeline? We have end-to-end ordering requirements for events.
- Please include an initial estimate for SLA credit for the window where we saw >2% errors. Our procurement team will request a formal statement.

I'll update when the allowlist rollout completes.

—Sam
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Retail

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.example>
Date: 2029-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Edge peering blackout — immediate customer switch plan

Hi Priyom,

We saw a partial control-plane flapping event impacting BGP session keepalives in north-1 between 07:52–08:10 PDT. Our engineering team has pushed a fix and sessions have been stable since ~08:14. We're pulling the BGP logs and will provide MTU/peer state traces to help with your postmortem. Ticket CI-3827 updated with logs.

If you need full packet captures, we can provide sanitized tcpdump slices for the 07:50–08:20 window — please confirm the target prefixes and we will deliver to your secure Drive link.

Regards,
CloudInfra Support

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.example>, Sam Patel <ops@acme.com>, CloudInfra Support <support@cloudinfra.example>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.example>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.example>
Date: 2029-05-31T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Edge peering blackout — immediate customer switch plan

Thanks all — short ops update and next steps.

1) Ordering guarantee: region_preference=any will preserve per-client session ordering for requests that are retried via our proxy; background jobs using at-least-once semantics should be fine, but if you have strict single-writer ordering constraints we recommend switching to the multi-region CNAME approach while we validate the proxy path. We'll follow up with a short test script you can run.

2) Packet capture & audit: CloudInfra, please deliver the sanitized tcpdump slices to the Drive link Priyom provided. Mina and I will validate sequence numbers and SNI to prove whether resets originated upstream or locally.

3) SLA credit path: Vanessa will coordinate the formal impact statement for Acme and include token-level error rates during the window 07:53–08:06. For now, expect a provisional credit estimate by EOD tomorrow.

4) Customer-facing checklist (for Acme):
   - Confirm allowlist application complete (reply to this thread)
   - Run the test script (we'll provide it) to verify end-to-end ordering
   - Let us know if you'd like a scheduled maintenance window to permanently update your DNS to the multi-region CNAME

We'll compile a post-incident packet-trace appendix and a one-page RCA next week.

-Karthik
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.example>
To: Sam Patel <ops@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.example>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.example>, CloudInfra Support <support@cloudinfra.example>
Date: 2029-06-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident: ingress blackout summary, packet evidence, and next steps

Sam — thanks for working through the rollouts. Attached is the preliminary post-incident brief (ingress_blackout_summary.pdf) and the routing script you asked for. Key takeaways:

- Root cause (preliminary): transient BGP session instability at CloudInfra north-1 leading to a subset of sessions withdrawing routes; this reduced effective capacity on our primary fabric and caused resets for IP-locked customers.
- Customer impact (Acme): elevated 5xx rate peaking at 2.7% across your ingestion endpoints between 07:54–08:04.
- Customer remediation completed: per your update we see allowlist changes applied at 08:05; your traffic fully migrated to our secondary fabric by 08:14 with ordering preserved per the runs we observed.

Next steps (owned):
- CloudInfra: deliver sanitized tcpdump as discussed (CI-3827) — target delivery 2029-06-03 EOD.
- Redwoods Reliability (Karthik/Mina): full RCA doc by 2029-06-07 including kernel-level socket state and control-plane timeline.
- Commercial (Vanessa): prepare provisional SLA credit proposal and get it to Acme procurement.

Sam — can you please confirm receipt of the attachments and whether you'd like us to schedule a 30-minute technical review next week to walk through the packet slices and ordering validation?

Attachment: ingress_blackout_summary.pdf (PDF, 220KB)
Attachment: customer-routing-script.sh (BASH, 2KB)

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
